sources.entry: SCM Manager - The easiest way to share and manage your Git, Mercurial and Subversion repositories over http. (Source Code) BSD-3-Clause Java/deb/Docker/K8S

summary.one_liner: SCM-Manager is a web-based tool for sharing and managing Git, Mercurial and Subversion repositories over HTTP, configured through its web interface.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes SCM-Manager as a central place to host and manage Git, Mercurial and Subversion repositories. It states that it needs no Apache and no database installation, and that users, groups and permissions are managed centrally. Configuration is done through the web interface rather than by editing config files. It offers a RESTful web service API with JSON and XML output, a simple plugin API, and a set of plugins. This branch (develop) is the development line; version 1.x lives on support/1.x. The README's development section covers building with Gradle, which requires JDK 25 and Git, with Mercurial needed for tests and Docker for the Docker package. Distribution packages (Docker, Helm, RPM, DEB, Windows) are built only when the enablePackaging property is set.
use_cases: manage Subversion repositories in a web UI
central user and permission management for source repos
host source code for a small team
how_to_run: Install Git, JDK 25, and Mercurial (for tests); Docker is needed only for the Docker package.
Clone the repository and check out the develop branch.
Start a development instance with: ./gradlew run (on Windows: gradlew.bat run).
Run all checks and tests with: ./gradlew build.
notable: Git, Mercurial and Subversion supported out of the box
No Apache or database installation required
Full RESTful API with JSON and XML responses
Configurable entirely from the web interface
caveats: Building from source requires JDK 25 and, for tests, a Mercurial install.
Packaging modules (Docker, Helm, RPM, DEB, Windows) are not built by default and need the enablePackaging property.
Publishing requires several credentials for package registries, Docker Hub, GitHub and GPG signing.
keywords: share git repos with my team
